data.narrative:
Vention, a Series C robotics and manufacturing platform founded by Etienne Lacroix and Max Windisch, has raised $95M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 9 comparables—1 public and 8 private companies—primarily in robotics and manufacturing at Series B through Series D stages, including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $156M total-raised proxy as a base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C progression, yielding $265M. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a $1.6B implied valuation, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer cohort includes both earlier-stage and later-stage funded companies, reflecting the volatility in robotics valuations.

The triangulated analysis supports a range from $225M to $1.9B, with a median of $958M. The wide spread reflects fundamental uncertainty around stage comparability—Vention sits at Series C while several peers are Series B (suggesting earlier-stage valuations anchored higher) or Series D (suggesting later-stage premium). The stage-progression method produces the most conservative estimate, while peer-median produces a substantially higher valuation. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers and the timing and terms of the next funding round.
